key_insight: I-GCM combines causal invariance testing with machine learning to prioritize candidate direct genetic and clinical determinants of complex traits, rather than cancer drug discovery specifically.
clinical_relevance: The framework could support therapeutic target prioritization, with JAK1 identified for severe COVID-19 in alignment with the clinical use of JAK1-targeting baricitinib.
method: Use PC-simple screening to narrow candidate variables.
Apply gradient-boosted trees within generalized covariance testing.
Test invariance across environments to identify candidate direct causes.
evidence_signal: Simulations with up to 3,000 variables and 50,000 samples achieved positive predictive values of approximately 0.84–1.00 and specificity ≥0.99; UK Biobank applications examined COVID-19 outcomes, HDL and triglycerides.
watch_item: Causal interpretations depend on modeling and environment assumptions; literature support does not substitute for experimental validation.
paper_title: A scalable invariant causal discovery framework reveals direct genetic and clinical determinants of complex human traits
